expected_evidence: Geological: multi-site sedimentary/'black mat' layer analyses at ~12,900 BP (Younger Dryas boundary, YDB) across North America showing failure to replicate reported carbon-spherule and magnetic-microspherule concentrations when independent labs reprocessed the same or nearby cores

Material: SEM/microscopy re-examination of purported spherules revealing terrestrial origins (fungal sclerotia, algal cysts, combustion char, industrial/laboratory contaminants, or rounded framboidal pyrite) rather than melt-glass or shock-metamorphosed impact ejecta

Geochemical/astronomical: absence of a consistent, reproducible platinum/iridium anomaly or extraterrestrial-He-3 signature at YDB layers across independent laboratories, and absence of a securely dated ~12.9 ka impact crater matching the proposed event
Material: failure to reproduce reported YDB nanodiamond concentrations under blind/independent testing protocols

Model-prior (scientific literature, e.g. Pinter et al. 2011 'Younger Dryas impact hypothesis: A requiem'; Daulton et al.; Holliday & Meltzer critiques): documented multi-team replication failures and methodological critiques of the original Firestone et al. 2007 claims
response.rationale: The event date (-10950) sits at the Younger Dryas onset boundary, so the relevant detectability row is ('younger-dryas', geological/material) rather than the unspecified period label. Refutation of an impact-ejecta claim is inherently a geological/material-science question: it depends on whether independent labs can re-sample the same stratigraphic horizons (black mats, paleosols) and re-run spherule counts, SEM shock-feature analysis, and geochemical (Ir/Pt) assays. These sediment layers are widespread, physically robust over ~13,000 years, and have in fact been repeatedly cored and tested by multiple independent research groups in the modern era, which is exactly the kind of high-preservation, high-replicability scenario the geological (0.65) and material (0.35, likely higher in practice for buried strata) rows anticipate. Textual, linguistic, oral_tradition, and iconographic channels are essentially irrelevant to a geochemical refutation and correctly score at/near zero for this period. I am drawing on model-prior (unverified, recalled from training rather than supplied evidence text) that this maps onto the real Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis controversy (Firestone et al. 2007 claims vs. Pinter et al. 2011 and related replication-failure literature); I flag this as low-tier unverified recollection, not established fact. Given that the underlying evidence type (sediment cores, microspherules, geochemical anomalies) is durable, geographically dispersed, and independently testable with modern lab techniques, absence-of-replication evidence is plausible to have been found rather than merely undetectable — supporting could_have_survived=true. I suggest nudging the effective aggregate detectability slightly above the raw geological/material baseline (to ~0.6) because this is a case where modern instrumentation (SEM, mass spectrometry) applied retrospectively to ancient strata dramatically increases detection power beyond what the baseline table (calibrated for artifact/settlement-type material evidence) assumes.
